interest: Illuminates Allied tensions between enforcing reparations and reviving Japanese steel amidst coal shortages and scrap metal demands.
overview: This file documents U.S. State Department and Allied administration of the Japanese iron and steel industry from June 1947 to December 1949 during the postwar occupation. It details Far Eastern Commission policies and SCAP directives extending the temporary retention of electric steel furnaces to alleviate severe coal shortages while balancing reparations claims. In addition, the records cover steel and pig iron allocations to the domestic textile machinery industry, North American commercial missions and proposals to survey and salvage Pacific scrap metal, private proposals regarding steel combines, and technical reports on fuel efficiency that supported record postwar production.
